passage:
A news app used AI to summarize long articles. It helped busy readers understand main points quickly.
However, a teacher showed students that summaries can leave out important details, uncertainty, or opposing views.
The class compared an AI summary with the full article. The summary was not wrong, but it was incomplete.
Students learned to use summaries as entrances, not exits.
A shortened text can save time, but it can also flatten complexity. Serious issues often live in details. Reading only summaries is like looking at a city from an airplane: useful for shape, poor for street life.
